newsitem.title: USA: CSCE coffee surges, May ends at 2-1/2-year high.
newsitem.headline: CSCE coffee surges, May ends at 2-1/2-year high.

text.p: CSCE coffee futures charged higher Wednesday, with spot May ending at more than a two-and-a-half-year high as speculators bought heavily after a monthly report showed a much lower-than-expected rise in consumer coffee stocks, traders said.

"A lot of people expected it to be higher," said Stephen Smith, the president of South Futures, a brokerage firm in Miami. "There were a lot of coffee shipments recently and that's what eveyone was watching.
May futures surged to a new life-of-contract high of 213.00 cents a lb during the day, but traders said a round of profit taking and producer selling trimmed gains.

May delivery finished at 208.05 cents, the highest level on the weekly charts since September 1994, up 15.65 cents -- or eight percent -- on the day. Second-month July soared 10.65 cents to 185.30 cents, while the back months closed up 6.00 to 8.25.
The May/July switch, a barometer of nearby availability, ballooned to 22.75 cents, up from 17.75 cents at the close on Tuesday.

The market gapped more than 10.00 cents higher at the opening this morning after Green Coffee Association of New York reported late Tuesday that supplies of green coffee stowed in U.S. warehouses rose in March by 111,000 60-kg bags to 1,657,000 bags.
"The GCA number was lower than expected," one trader said, "and the open showed there were a lot of people very short going into this number."

Most analysts had forecast an increase of between 250,000 and 300,000 bags, with some operators looking for a build of up to 700,000 bags, after Latin America shipped heavily over the last several weeks to take advantage of higher futures prices.
While the GCA figures may have been way below expectations, some market participants pointed out that the GCA figures do not take into account stocks at roaster plants and finished products.

"Roasters have been building stocks and have a lot of finished products," said South Future's Smith. "They got caught out dramatically in the December and March positions and I have to believe thay have taken protection and tried to build a little cushion to go through the (Brazil) frost season."
News a strike by stevedores in at the key Brazilian port of Santos is set to spread nationally at midnight Thursday for 48 hours also fuelled bullish sentiment, traders said.
Nerves were further rattled by news of a Colombian truck drivers' strike set for April 20.

Technically, traders said after today's strong close they look for May to test today's high of 213.00 cents, with the next upside objective near 220.00. Support was seen at 205.00 cents, then 200.00 cents.

But while bullish technicals and fundamentals to could lead to further gains, some traders warned that soaring futures prices could prompt roasters to raise retail prices again, which could hurt consumption.
"If it stay at these levels, roasters will have to raise prices," one trader said. "That could affect consumption."

After Tuesday's close, CSCE reported certified coffee stocks were down 750 60-kg bags, to 80,078 bags as of April 15. There were no bags pending grading, the exchange said. ((--Patricia Avidan, New York Commodity Desk +1 212 859 1640))
